advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the ndjson import close intentionally bypasses the completion-verification close gate now (old `force=True` did not); if not, pass a value that only satisfies the start-work intent or gate the bypass to the child-safety-net case.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/txn.py: `if target_status == "closed" and force_reason: status_data["force_close_reason"] = force_reason` — persisted only when force reason truthy

Old param `force: bool` armed only the start-work gate; the close path keyed on the now-removed `force_close`, so the pre-change `force=True` on a `-> closed` import close left the completion gate un-bypassed. The migration description calls this a mechanical call-site migration, suggesting the semantic change may be unintended.
advisory.finding: NDJSON import close now bypasses the completion-verification close gate where it previously did not. The old call `transition_compute(..., "open", "closed", force=True, ...)` set only the start-work `force` bool; the close-gate bypass keyed on the separate `force_close` param (defaulted ""), so a `-> closed` transition did NOT bypass the completion gate. The migrated call passes `force_reason="ndjson import safety net"`, which `transition_compute` funnels through `force_close=_force_note(force_reason)` and thus DOES bypass the close gate, and additionally records a `force_close_reason` key + FORCE_CLOSE audit comment on every imported close.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `transition(force="")` behave identically to `claim(force="")` (either both bypass or both do not) so the documented parity holds.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:387: `if force_reason is None: return ""` then `return force_reason or "(no reason given)"` — empty string maps to the placeholder (forces)
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:401: `_transition.claim_compute(resolved, assignee=assignee, force_reason=force or "", ...)` — claim maps empty string to "" (does NOT force)
src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:258: `if force_reason:` — gate bypasses only on a truthy string
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:270-280 docstring claims force is 'shaped exactly like claim's'
advisory.finding: Library-level force parity between `claim` and `transition` diverges for an empty-string force value. `claim(force="")` forwards `force or ""` -> `force_reason=""`, which the plan-review gate treats as NOT forcing (no bypass). `transition(force="")` normalizes to `""` then `_force_note("")` returns `"(no reason given)"`, which DOES bypass. The docstrings assert the two verbs are 'spelled identically', but `force=""` behaves oppositely.
